title: Capture the Resolution
subtitle: The fix and the category-as-worked
scenario: TKT-4001 is resolved - Tier-2 restarted the checkout service. Capture the outcome, including the category it turned out to be when actually worked. On a clean ticket the worked category matches the assigned one, but you always record it, because that is what makes misroute detection possible.
input: TKT-4001 (assigned category outage) was resolved by the Tier-2 Engineer, who restarted the checkout service. When actually worked, it was indeed an outage. Capture the fix, the worked category, and who resolved it.
instructions: Record the category it was actually worked as (workedCategory).
Record who resolved it, then validate.
copilotPrompt: Build one JSON resolution record for TKT-4001: fix 'restarted the checkout service', workedCategory 'outage', resolvedBy 'Tier-2 Engineer'.
successMessage: Resolution captured. The worked category is recorded so misroutes can be caught.
editorHelper: Record the fix - and the category it actually was.

intro.heading: Before you learn: capture the outcome

sections.title: The fix is the record
sections.body: A resolved ticket without a captured fix teaches nothing. Recording what actually solved it - 'restarted the checkout service' - is what a future agent (or the digest) can rely on.

sections.title: Category-as-worked is ground truth
sections.body: The category a ticket was assigned is a hypothesis; the category it was actually worked as is the truth. Capturing the worked category is the whole basis for catching misroutes.

sections.title: Match today, mismatch tomorrow
sections.body: This ticket was correctly an outage, so worked matches assigned. You still record it - because the value of the field is exactly the days it does NOT match.

sections.title: What you produce here
sections.body: A resolution record the misroute check compares against the assigned category.

fieldGuide.meaning: The category it was actually worked as.

realWorld.soloRebuildPath: You'd write the fix in the ticket and tag what it really was, so patterns and misroutes surface later.

tools.powerAutomate: set the resolution and worked-category fields on close
tools.zapier: update the ticket with the fix and true category

takeaway.heading: Resolution captured
points: You recorded the fix that resolved the ticket.
You captured the category-as-worked, the ground truth for misroutes.
Worked matched assigned here - but you record it every time.
The misroute check compares this against the assigned category.
The workflow can now capture outcomes that feed learning.
